newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bankers see 1996 CPI at 19.5 pct -poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish bankers see 1996 CPI at 19.5 pct -poll.

text.p: Polish banks have lowered in October their 1996 consumer inflation forecast to 19.5 percent from 19.9 percent predicted last month, a survey of 208 banking managers by the private polling institute Pentor, showed.
Official statistical office figures released earlier on Tuesday showed year-on-year inflation in September at 19.5 percdent.
A Reuter poll of analysts at Poland's 26 largest banks earlier this month showed they expected year-on-year inflation to fall to 18.74 percent in December.
The government's 1996 price growth target is 17 percent. @

Pentor also said the polled bankers expected the Polish zloty to fall to about 2.82 to the dollar by the end of the year, down from last month's forecast of 2.81 and unchanged from Tuesday's fixing of 2.8210 zlotys.
The Reuter poll showed bankers expected the zloty to ease to 2.8768 against the dollar by December 31, 1996.
